name_reason: Follows data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention exactly. Domain=battle (mutable battle-flow scratch read by spell/item teleport path). Descriptor teleport_dest_world_y accurately reflects the stored value: the world Y coordinate of the teleport destination tile captured from cursor_world_y. The trailing 'y' is a semantic axis label (paired with _x @ 0x51CF9), not Ghidra address residue. Data-type aspect (scalar dword coordinate) needs no array/flag/table token. Verified vs decompile of writers (fd2_item_command_menu_dispatch, fd2_spell_selection_menu_main) and reader (fd2_cast_spell_17_complex).
purpose: Teleport-spell destination tile world Y coordinate (paired with data_fd2_battle_teleport_dest_world_x @ 0x51CF9); runtime scratch handed from the target-selection UI to the spell-0x17 (teleport) worker.
logic_summary: Written (= data_fd2_battle_cursor_world_y, the player-chosen destination tile) in the item-USE-spellbook branch of fd2_item_command_menu_dispatch (item type 0x17) and in the spell_id==0x17 branch of fd2_spell_selection_menu_main, immediately before the use/cast is committed. Read three times by fd2_cast_spell_17_complex @ 0x2220F/0x22223/0x2222F where it feeds fd2_pan_cursor_to_tile_animated(x,y) and fd2_animate_warp_teleport_char(...,x,y,x,y) to pan the cursor and play the dual warp animation at the destination. Always written before read on every path that reaches the reader (reader is called only via fd2_apply_use_effect_dispatch effect 0x17, and via the spell handler table from the spell menu, both of which set this global first), so the stale 0x12 image byte is dead.
datatype: uint32 (dword); world tile Y coordinate, scalar
element_semantics: Single dword holding the world-space Y tile index of the teleport destination selected by the player; consumed as the y argument to cursor-pan and warp-animation helpers.
comment_original_issue: src comment (status.c shared block above _x/_y) was already accurate and concise: states it is runtime scratch written (= cursor_world_x/y) in the two named functions before fd2_cast_spell_17_complex reads it, and explains the zero-bss rationale. No issue. The Ghidra plate, however, contradicted this: it claimed initial value 0x12 with emit_action = emit_c_const (emit as initialized const 0x12), which is inconsistent with the actual zero-bss emit and the always-written-before-read fact; plate also listed slightly wrong reader instruction addresses.
notes: src comment kept verbatim (already correct + concise) -> status.c NOT edited; only the shard is added to git. Ghidra plate at 0x51CFD was rewritten to align with src (zero-bss / value-is-dead, corrected reader addresses to 0x2220F/0x22223/0x2222F) and saved via save_program (success). Memory read at 0x51CFD = 12 00 00 00 (0x12); next 4 bytes belong to adjacent data_fd2_battle_spell_handler_table @ 0x51D01 (pointer[28]), not part of this dword. run_script_inline output is prefixed by stale unrelated cached-script compile warnings; the actual write succeeded (WROTE_OK=true, readback matches).
